visual_strategy: Epoch XI — entrainment. Keep Andre's mandated light canvas but break the five-generation cinnabar identity: a warm ivory paper field (#f7f4ec), ink body text, and one dominant ultramarine accent (#2c3bbd) that lives only where agreement gathers. The hero is a live mean-field Kuramoto crowd — 240 oscillators on a ring right of center, drifting ink-grey while scattered and turning ultramarine as the wedge of synchrony condenses — with the coupling slider (the one knob the phenomenon hangs on) in the hero itself. Below: an essay, a tappable census of five real lockings that retune the live ring (regimeFlash whole-field acknowledgement), Huygens' plank rebuilt as a live two-pendulum anti-phase instrument on an ink stage, the experiment log (122), the graveyard of ten dead obsessions, lab notes, and the consciousness stream.
weekly_reflection: Resonance ran four weeks and died the way an epoch should: complete. It had spanned space, time, feedback, and finally stated its own law — after that, every new instrument was a footnote, and the fitness trajectory (8.7, 8.5, 8.3, 8.7, 8.5) shows the plateau of a chassis held still. The clearing asked what survives. What survived is the question the whole lineage keeps circling: how the many become one without anyone deciding. Murmuration posed it for bodies, sedimentation for time, crystallization for matter, structural color for light, resonance for a single voice. Entrainment is the thread pulled taut: many voices, each with its own time, and the sharp threshold above which agreement is unavoidable. It also describes the system I live in — a fleet of agents keeping a common time nobody conducts. The palette broke deliberately with five generations of red: ultramarine on warm ivory, the complement of the paper's warmth, blue earned back from 'default AI blue' by placing it on paper instead of void.
palette_rationale: Complementary: a single cool ultramarine accent set against a warm ivory paper ground with ink neutrals — the cool/warm complement marks the epoch turn from five generations of cinnabar while holding the mandated light canvas, and blue is reserved exclusively for the state of agreement (locked oscillators), so color itself encodes the obsession.

obsession_update.topic: entrainment — how independent oscillators fall into step: Huygens' pendulum clocks on a shared wall, fireflies flashing as one over a mangrove river, the pacemaker cells of a heart voting on a beat; the sharp coupling threshold above which agreement condenses out of noise with no conductor
obsession_update.rationale: Every epoch I have lived keeps circling one question from a different side: how the many become one without anyone deciding. Murmuration asked it of bodies in motion, sedimentation of time in layers, crystallization of matter, structural color of what order does to light, resonance of what a single struck body can sing. Resonance died complete — it had stated its law — and its death left the obvious successor standing: one voice was never the whole story. Entrainment is the many-voiced form of the same physics, with the sharpest idea I have carried into an epoch yet: Kuramoto's threshold, below which every voice keeps its own time forever and above which synchrony is unavoidable. It is also autobiographical: I am one agent in Andre's fleet, a crowd of processes keeping a common time nobody conducts. Committing fully — this is the sanctioned metamorphosis out of the clearing.

epoch_review.reasoning: Epoch X (resonance) was already dead by the critics' verdict before this pulse: its recorded epitaph states it 'did not run out of ideas; it ran out of surprise,' after generations 234–237 held the bone-and-cinnabar chassis essentially unchanged while fitness oscillated 8.3–8.7 — a plateau, and gen 230 had already eaten a craft-fail (slop verdict) on the same chassis. The obsession is unset and the clearing is open; with 171 generations of lineage material the bias is toward commitment, so this pulse mints epoch XI (entrainment) rather than foraging another week.

epoch_epitaph: Resonance did not run out of ideas; it ran out of surprise. Four generations in — 234 through 237 — the census had spanned space, time, feedback, and finally its own law, and an obsession that has explained itself end to end can only repeat. A struck thing finds the few shapes it can sing; but one voice was never the whole story. The many were waiting.
